title: Making progress on our pixel art model!
author: HugoDzz
selftext: Sharing some progress since last week's samples! ([wolf, plant, and skeleton](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/s/hTibjWCtwO) samples). Also shipped a rock-solid prompt-based editing mode!

replies.author: RickDripps
replies.body: Yup, looks kind of expensive for what it is too...

comments.author: speps
comments.body: They don’t even look the same at different scales 🤔

replies.author: Kalaminator
replies.body: I mean, it is obvious that you lose or get detail by downscaling or upscaling, but it doesn't make sense to change color hue on details, or for example, on the burger to he the cheese in one direction and have cheese in a different direction on the other scales, etc. There should be continuity.

replies.author: Elegant-Tangerine198
replies.body: This is absolutely fine. You want variety in generations. Each generation should be a fresh new run rather than a scaling of an predetermined picture. That's why.

replies.author: Itadorijin
replies.body: idk man seems like a limitation to me. changing resolution or scale shouldnt change the sprite beyond the extra detail

replies.author: Elegant-Tangerine198
replies.body: Could you tell me where you feel limited? Consider when you have a good generation at 32x32 and you want a 64x64 version, you can use some existing upscaling methods instead. This will not change sprite details. If you don't like the 32x32 one and want to start fresh at 64x64, use the generation model. Would this help?

comments.author: Pulkownik
comments.body: I want to test it out! 🥳
